aboutRicardo.title: Ricardo Faya
paragraphs: With more than 28 years in media and technology, Ricardo Faya is one of Brazil's pioneers in Artificial Intelligence education.
His journey began as a professional video editor, working at international companies like Fox International Channels and leading teams at FGV as Editor in Chief.
In 2020, after seeing AI's transformational potential, he started an intensive study journey, earning Google Cloud certifications in Generative AI, Machine Learning, and Prompt Engineering.
Today he is fully dedicated to helping professionals and companies master AI tools through a practical, results-driven approach.

Resources.ctaTitle: Want more than the free material?
Resources.ctaText: FayAI courses take the same content and turn it into guided practice, with a project, a quiz and a certificate. The first lesson of every course is open.

CoursesByTool.title: Courses by tool
CoursesByTool.intro: The same question arrives every week: "I want to learn ChatGPT, where do I start?". This page answers it by grouping the catalogue by the tool each course actually teaches — not by topic, by the tool you will have open on screen while you study.
CoursesByTool.summary: {courses} active courses, grouped into {tools} tools. The first lesson of every course is open, so you can check the pace before deciding.
CoursesByTool.genericNote: Courses built around {tool}. Each one walks through the steps inside the tool itself, with the examples running — not just the theory behind it.

toolNotes.chatgpt: The most used tool and the most wasted one: almost everyone treats it as a search box. These courses go from the basic prompt to professional use — context, role, output format, custom GPTs, and the tasks where ChatGPT still gets it wrong and you have to check.
toolNotes.claude: Claude has the edge on long text, document analysis and working alongside code. These courses cover safe use inside a company, collaborating with the model, and what changes compared to ChatGPT day to day.
toolNotes.gemini: Google model, and the practical difference is where it lives: inside Gmail, Docs, Sheets and Drive. The course treats Gemini as part of the workflow you already have, not as a separate website.
toolNotes.perplexity: Research with cited sources instead of answers with no trail. It suits anyone who has to verify, compare and deliver material with provenance — and the course also shows how to check what the tool brought back.
toolNotes.midjourney: Image generation for people who need consistent results, not luck. Framing, lighting, style reference, and building a prompt you can repeat tomorrow and get the same standard.
toolNotes.openclaw: An open alternative that runs under your own control. It matters to anyone who cannot send data outside, or who wants to understand what happens beneath the interface of the closed tools.
toolNotes.autoresearch: Automated research in a loop: the machine proposes, tests, measures and keeps what improved. It is the method behind much of what FayAI publishes.
toolNotes.multi-plataforma: Courses that are not tied to a single tool, because real work is not either: part in ChatGPT, part in Claude, part in an automation. Choosing between them is taught along the way.
toolNotes.multi-tool: Courses that are not tied to a single tool, because real work is not either: part in ChatGPT, part in Claude, part in an automation. Choosing between them is taught along the way.
toolNotes.multi-framework: Agent and automation courses that span more than one framework. What you learn here outlives the next fashionable library.
toolNotes.n8n: Visual automation you host yourself: boxes joined by arrows instead of code, running on your own machine or server. It is the shortest path between "I do this by hand every week" and "this happens on its own".
toolNotes.make: Cloud automation with hundreds of apps ready to connect. Good for wiring together the tools you already use — spreadsheet, email, CRM, WhatsApp — without maintaining any server.
toolNotes.langchain: The scaffolding under most agents: memory, tools, chaining steps and reading documents. Learning it means learning the vocabulary the other frameworks copied.
toolNotes.docker: Not an AI tool — it is what makes yours run the same way everywhere. It shows up in the courses where the model, the vector database and the interface come up together and stop depending on whatever was installed on your machine.
toolNotes.leonardo ai: Image generation with fine control over style and community-trained models. It suits anyone who needs volume with a consistent visual identity: campaign assets, covers, a character that keeps coming back.

items.question: What is FayAi?
items.answer: FayAi is a complete AI education platform, offering practical courses, AI tools and specialized consulting for professionals and companies.

items.question: Do I need prior programming knowledge?
items.answer: No! Our courses are designed for all levels. We have specific tracks for beginners that don't require prior technical knowledge.

items.question: How does course access work?
items.answer: After enrollment, you have immediate access to all course content through our portal. Access is lifetime for paid courses.

items.question: What payment methods are accepted?
items.answer: We accept credit cards (Visa, Mastercard), PIX and bank slip. We offer up to 12 interest-free installments.

items.question: Is there a refund guarantee?
items.answer: Yes! We offer a 7-day guarantee. If you're not satisfied, we refund 100% of the amount invested.

items.question: Can I cancel my subscription anytime?
items.answer: Yes, you can cancel your subscription whenever you want. Your access remains active until the end of the already paid period.

items.question: What is Studio AI?
items.answer: Studio AI is our AI-powered image generation tool. You can create unique art using text prompts.

items.question: How many images can I generate?
items.answer: Free users can generate 1 image. Paid plans have higher limits: Starter (50/month), Pro and Business (unlimited).

items.question: Can I use the images commercially?
items.answer: Yes! All images generated in Studio AI are your property and can be used commercially.

HelpCenter.stepsTitle: Starting from scratch, in five steps
HelpCenter.stepsIntro: If this is your first time here, this is the shortest path between opening the site and having watched a lesson. No step requires payment.

steps.title: Open a free lesson before creating an account
steps.text: The first lesson of every course in the catalogue is open and asks for no sign-up. Use it to check the pace, the depth and whether the way we explain things suits you — before deciding anything.

steps.title: Create the account with the email you actually use
steps.text: Your email is what ties together your enrolment, your progress and your certificate. Changing it later is possible but tedious: start with the address you will still be reading a year from now.

steps.title: Pick a course and finish one chapter
steps.text: Progress is saved per chapter, automatically. You can stop halfway, close the browser and come back the next day at the exact point where you left off, from any device.

steps.title: Take the quiz when you finish
steps.text: Every course has a question bank drawn from the content you have just read. Score above the required minimum and the certificate is issued immediately, with a public verification code.

steps.title: Tailor the material in the Atelier
steps.text: Inside a course, under My / Settings, you can adjust the depth and the length of the text for your own context. The material rewrites itself for you without changing the course for anyone else.

HelpCenter.troubleTitle: Common problems, and what to do

trouble.q: I logged in but the course I bought is not in my list
trouble.a: Check that you are signed in with the same email you used at checkout — that is the cause in almost every case. If it is the same address, contact support with the email and the purchase date: the enrolment may have been left inactive, and reactivating takes minutes.

trouble.q: The site switched back to Portuguese on its own
trouble.a: That happens when an older link carries no language and navigation falls back to your browser default. Switch with the language selector at the top: the address then starts with /en and stays that way as you browse.

trouble.q: I finished the quiz and no certificate arrived
trouble.a: The certificate is only issued above the course pass mark. Retake the quiz — questions are drawn from a larger bank, so the second attempt is not the same exam. If you did pass and still received nothing, check the certificate verification page before opening a ticket.
It is nearly always a stale browser cache. Reload with Ctrl+Shift+R (Cmd+Shift+R on Mac). If it persists, try a private window: if it works there, an extension is blocking the media.
Use password recovery on the login screen. The link arrives by email and expires — if it is slow, check the spam folder before requesting another, because a new request invalidates the previous link.

method.title: How the material is made
method.intro: A FayAI course is not a script recorded in an afternoon. The process is the same in all of them, and it is what holds quality up while the faculty stays small.

items.title: Research before writing
items.text: Every course starts with a round of primary-source research: official documentation, product changelogs, papers and tests run in-house. What goes into the text has a traceable origin — no "people say".

items.title: Every number has a source
items.text: Prices, limits, context sizes and release dates are checked before publishing. A number without a source does not go in, because that is exactly the kind of error that ages a course in three months and takes trust in the rest with it.

items.title: Text measured against repetition
items.text: Before publishing, the material is measured for repeated paragraphs. A course padded with variations of the same sentence passes any shallow review and teaches nothing; here it does not pass the gate.

items.title: Practice, quiz and certificate
items.text: Every course ends in an exercise and a question bank drawn from its own content. The certificate is only issued above the pass mark, and carries a public verification code.

items.title: Updated when the tool changes
items.text: New model, new price, a feature that disappeared: the course is reviewed and whatever aged is rewritten. Anyone who already bought it gets the updated version at no extra cost.

Glossary.title: Artificial Intelligence Glossary
Glossary.description: Understand the main terms and concepts of the AI world.

terms.definition: Application Programming Interface. Allows different systems to communicate with each other.
A system that uses AI to plan and execute multiple steps or tools toward a goal.
Use of rules and tools to perform repetitive tasks with little manual intervention.
OpenAI's language model capable of generating human-like text in conversations.
AI assistant developed by Anthropic, focused on safety and usefulness.
Arrangement of elements and empty space in an image to guide attention.
Information about scenario, audience and goal that helps AI answer appropriately.
Numerical representation of text that captures its semantic meaning.
Process of adjusting a pre-trained model for a specific task.
Generative Pre-trained Transformer. OpenAI's language model architecture.
A rule or limit that reduces errors, risks and unwanted AI behavior.
When an AI model generates false or invented information that appears true.
Breaking a request into clear parts such as subject, context, style, composition and format.
Large Language Model. Language models trained on large amounts of text.
Amount of information a model can consider at once during a conversation.
A model or workflow that can work with text, images, audio, video or other modalities.
Open-source workflow automation and integration platform.
Instruction or question given to an AI model to guide its response.
The art of creating effective prompts to get better results from AI models.
Ability to link a claim to the source or evidence that supports it.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Combines information retrieval with text generation.
Basic unit of text processed by language models (can be a word or part of it).
A control that usually changes how varied and unpredictable a model's response is.
Neural network architecture that revolutionized natural language processing.
Database optimized for storing and searching vector embeddings.
A systematic tendency that can favor or harm groups, ideas or results.
Ability of a model to perform tasks without prior specific examples.

why.d: In a game a mistake costs a point; in a work prompt it costs your afternoon. Every round puts you in front of the same decision you meet in real life — which ingredient the prompt is missing, which claim is a myth, which instruction produced that image — with no consequence attached.

A round lasts under a minute and answers you immediately. That short loop between trying and finding out is what makes the pattern stick; reading the same rule in a paragraph does not do the same thing.

why.t: The same games continue inside the platform
why.d: These are the portal games, opened here with no sign-up. With an account they start earning XP, join your history and link to the courses covering the same ground.
